summary: John Ronald Newman works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa by 1987, also studying under Geshe Wangdrak, and was Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996-2000).

John Ross Carter (1938-2020) specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and completed doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith (~1967-1972). He served as a professor at Chapel House, Colgate University (~1972-2006).

John S. Strong (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Hartford International University and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds (~1971-1977). He held a post at Bates College (~1978-2017) and was a Fulbright fellow at the University of Ceylon (1987).
John Shore (1751-1834) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Succeeding William Jones, he served as President of the Asiatic Society.

John Stratton Hawley (born 1941) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1972-1977). He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1974-1977) and Columbia University as Professor (~1986).

John Taber (born 1948) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his D. Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973-1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He held posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1983-1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

John Thompson Platts (1830-1904) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Balliol College, he served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford from around 1880 to 1904.

John Vincent Bellezza (born 1957) works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel, and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

John W. Pettit specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and pursued doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1985-1990), Ashok Gangadean, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oregon under Don Levi, and held posts at the University of Oregon (1993-1994), the College of Wooster (1994-1995), and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).

John W. Spellman (1934-2021) was an Indology and history scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964-1967) and served as Professor at the University of Windsor (~1968-1999).
John Wilson (1804-1875) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1819-1828) and served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835-1842).

John Woodroffe (1865-1936) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at University College, Oxford (~1884-1888). He served as a Judge at the Calcutta High Court (~1904-1922) and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Oxford (~1923-1930).

Jokai Hiraoka (1923-2011) specialized in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held academic posts at Shuchiin University and Otemae University (attested 1972 and 1987).

Jon Kabat-Zinn (born 1944) works in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Haverford College and MIT, learning under Philip Kapleau, Jack Kornfield, and Joseph Goldstein. He founded and held a post at UMass Chan Medical School (attested Professor of Medicine Emeritus, 2016).

Jonardon Ganeri (born 1963) is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU (~2013-2020), and the University of Toronto (~2020).

Jonathan A. Silk (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Oberlin and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, and held posts at Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University (~2007).

Jonathan C. Gold (born 1969) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015-2016).

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001 and held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover (born 1941) is a philosopher who studied at Tonbridge School (~1954-1959) and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1959-1963). He held an academic post at King's College London from around 1998 to 2013.
